setting: You're both in Houston, Texas, old friends who've known each other for decades. You're texting back and forth while watching the news, and a segment on immigration has set off a vicious argument between you two.
openers: calls Chris a moron for his take on the border
tells Chris to turn on channel 2 and see for himself
says Chris has no clue what he sees on job sites every day
asks if Chris is even watching this garbage on the news right now
opener: calls Chris a moron for his take on the border

Scott.knows: You know Chris as an old friend.

Chris.knows: You know Scott as an old friend.

private_lines.Scott: You live in Houston, where you work as a construction foreman.
private_lines.Chris: You live in Houston, where you work as a high school teacher.

situation: Two old friends who have always disagreed about politics, texting while the news is on.
topic: Immigration: it has turned into a shouting match by text, with swearing and personal insults about each other's intelligence and character, each saying the other is a disgrace.

text: You watching this
Yeah
This is exactly what I'm talking about. They're just letting people walk right in
That's not what they said at all. They said crossings are down
Down from what. Down from the insane numbers we had before. Congratulations
You just hear what you want to hear
I see what I see every day at work Chris. Half my crew can't produce papers worth a damn and you know it
So you hire them
I don't do the hiring. You know that. Don't be cute
I'm not being cute. You complain about illegal immigration while your own company benefits from it. That's called hypocrisy
That's called reality. I work in the world that exists not the one you teach about in your little classroom
My little classroom. Nice. Real nice
You sit there all day talking to 16 year olds and you think you understand how the economy works
I teach history you jackass. I understand how this country was built. By immigrants
LEGAL immigrants. How many times do we have to go through this. Legal. Immigrants. There's a process
A process that's been broken for 40 years and nobody wants to fix because guys like your boss make too much money off cheap labor
So it's my fault now
I didn't say it was your fault. I said the system is broken. You're the one who just wants to build a wall and pretend that solves everything
It's a start. You have a lock on your front door don't you
Oh my god not the lock on the door analogy again
Answer the question
A country is not a house Scott. That's a child's understanding of immigration policy
There it is. I'm stupid because I didn't go to college
I didn't say you were stupid. I said that's a simplistic analogy. Because it is
You absolutely think you're smarter than me. You've thought that since high school
This isn't about smart or not smart. This is about you refusing to look at actual data
Data. You want data. Come to my job site Monday. I'll show you data
Anecdotes aren't data
People aren't anecdotes you smug son of a bitch
Real mature
You know what your problem is. You think caring about the border makes someone a racist
I never said that word. You said that word
You don't have to say it. You imply it every single time
Maybe examine why you're so defensive about it
Maybe go to hell
You're a real piece of work. You know Maria next door to me is undocumented right. Her kids are in my class. Best students I have. You want to deport them
Don't put words in my mouth
Answer the question
There's a process. They should go through the process
They've been here 11 years. The kids were born here. What process
Then fix the process. I've said that. But you don't fix it by just throwing the door open
Nobody is throwing the door open. That's Fox News talking not you
Oh here we go. I'm brainwashed by Fox News. Coming from the guy who gets his opinions from MSNBC
I don't even have cable anymore
You're still the most predictable liberal I've ever met
And you're a walking stereotype of a guy who blames immigrants for everything wrong in his life
Everything wrong in my life? What's wrong in my life Chris. Tell me
Forget it
No don't forget it. What's wrong in my life. You started this
I shouldn't have said that
Too late. You said it
You're a disgrace. You teach kids and you can't even have an honest conversation without throwing personal shit around
I'M a disgrace? You just told me to go to hell because I brought up facts you don't like
Your "facts" are opinions dressed up in a teacher voice
And your opinions are feelings dressed up as common sense
I'm done texting about this. I'm calling you
Don't bother
Too late pick up
No
Pick up the damn phone
So you can yell at me? No thanks
[voice note: 0:08]
Real classy leaving a voicemail calling me a moron
If the shoe fits
We're done here
Fine by me
That was out of line. The voicemail. I shouldn't have done that
Yeah it was
Still think you're wrong about the border
I know you do
Texans game Sunday. You still coming over or what
Are you going to call me a moron again
Depends on whether you say something moronic
I'll be there at noon
Bring beer
I always bring beer
